programme.title: Scotland: Rome's Final Frontier
programme.desc: Were the ancient Scottish tribes too much for the Roman Empire? Or was Scotland simply not worth conquering? Archaeologist Dr Fraser Hunter looks back on three centuries of contact and conflict with Scotland’s Roman invaders. The first Tay Bridge, the first depiction of tartan and forgotten Roman camps that once held 35,000 men. A story of a superpower pitted against tribesmen and warlords, and one with fascinating modern parallels.

programme.title: Treasures of the Anglo-Saxons
programme.desc: Art historian Dr Nina Ramirez reveals the codes and messages hidden in Anglo-Saxon art. From the beautiful jewellery that adorned the first violent pagan invaders through to the stunning Christian manuscripts they would become famous for, she explores the beliefs and ideas that shaped Anglo-Saxon art. Examining many of the greatest Anglo-Saxon treasures - such as the Sutton Hoo artefacts, the Staffordshire hoard, the Franks Casket and the Lindisfarne Gospels - Dr Ramirez charts 600 years of artistic development which was stopped dead in its tracks by the Norman Conquest.

programme.title: Omnibus

The film was made during rehearsals for the UK premiere of Sunday in the Park with George, which won the Olivier Award for best musical in 1991.

programme.title: Stephen Sondheim’s Old Friends
programme.desc: On 3 May 2022, Cameron Mackintosh invited many of Stephen Sondheim’s old friends to join him in London’s West End for a thrilling, joyously staged production. He had specially devised it to celebrate Sondheim’s extraordinary talents as a composer and lyricist. Featuring an all-star cast including Michael Ball, Helena Bonham Carter, Rob Brydon, Petula Clark, Anna-Jane Casey, Rosalie Craig, Janie Dee, Judi Dench, Daniel Evans, Maria Friedman, Haydn Gwynne, Bonnie Langford, Damian Lewis and Julia McKenzie.

programme.title: Sondheim at the BBC
programme.desc: A celebration of the work of one of the great songwriters and lyricists, Stephen Sondheim, who passed away in November 2021 at the age of 91. A giant of musical theatre, Sondheim first found international fame in 1957 as the lyricist for Leonard Bernstein’s West Side Story and would inspire generations from that moment on. This selection includes some of Sondheim’s finest songs, broadcast on the BBC over a period of 60 years, with performances from a cast of his friends and fans that features some of the biggest names of stage and screen, including Shirley Bassey, Sammy Davis Jr, Michael Ball and Liza Minnelli.

programme.title: The Stuarts
programme.desc: The final, dramatic act of the Stuart century saw the Stuarts fatally divided by religion: brother versus brother, and two daughters supporting the overthrow of their father. After Charles II's brother, the Catholic James VII and II, was deposed by protestant William of Orange in 1688, Britain became a constitutional monarchy. However, the so-called 1688 'Glorious Revolution' came at a price, as Scotland lost her sovereignty and became part of Great Britain in 1707, whilst Ireland had been reduced from a kingdom to a colony. The politics of resentment has continued to trouble Ireland until the present day.

programme.title: Voyage to Mars: The Longest Goodbye
programme.desc: Nasa intends to send astronauts to Mars. To succeed, crew members will have to overcome unprecedented, life-threatening challenges, and while many of these hazards are physical, the most elusive are psychological. Throughout the expected three-year absence, crew members won’t be able to communicate with Earth in real time due to the immense distance. The psychological impact of this level of disconnectedness and isolation – both from mission control and loved ones – is impossible to predict and endangers the mission itself. Directed to mitigate this threat is Dr Al Holland, a Nasa psychologist whose job is to keep astronauts mentally stable in space. The Longest Goodbye follows Holland, rookie astronauts Kayla Barron and Matthias Maurer and former astronaut Cady Coleman, among others, as they grapple with the tension between their dream of reaching new frontiers and the basic human need to stay connected to home.

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: A weekly programme from the BBC World Service, bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world by BBC Eye, the World Service's critically acclaimed investigative unit, and featuring expert global correspondents getting to the heart of the biggest international stories. In this episode: Tim Whewell reports from eastern Libya, where a vast reconstruction programme led by the Haftar family is transforming cities and reshaping the country's political future. As new roads, housing projects and landmarks emerge, we examine whether stability and development are outweighing concerns about accountability and democratic change. Plus: we follow Zaher, a young Sudanese boy whose life was changed by war when a drone strike left him severely injured. A year on, we meet him in Cairo as he learns to walk with prosthetic limbs and begins rebuilding a childhood interrupted by conflict.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: As Grand Theft Auto VI is released after more than a decade of development and many months of hype, we look at how a Scottish video game became one of the world's most successful, and most profitable, entertainment franchises. We talk to Brian Baglow who worked on the original GTA title and now leads the Scottish Games Network and Cara Ellison who worked on GTA IV and is now an award-winning games developer. Ian Rumsey from ITN tells us about his role as CEO of one of the UK's biggest TV news providers. The rise of social media is reshaping how court cases are reported. Media law expert Sian Harrison and criminal barrister Andrew Taylor assess how online influencers are entering courtrooms, the challenges this poses for contempt of court laws and how digital commentary by high-profile defendants is testing long-standing legal boundaries.

programme.title: The Interface
programme.desc: Could an AI ever be conscious? And if it were, how would we know? Thomas Germain and Jessica Maddox put the question to philosopher Jeff Sebo, director of the Center for Mind, Ethics, and Policy at New York University. Jeff isn't claiming AI is conscious, and he's clear that nobody knows for sure. His argument is that the possibility is real enough to study properly and plan for now, rather than scrambling after the fact as we did with animals and the climate. He explains what consciousness and sentience actually mean, why 'it's just software' doesn't settle the matter, and why the very idea makes so many people so angry. Thomas and Jess push back with the big objections. Shouldn't we fix the problems facing humans first? And can we trust AI companies to give us straight answers?

programme.desc: Highlights of seven Premier League games, including leaders Arsenal, who travel to Newcastle. programme.title: Sunday Morning Live
programme.desc: Sean Fletcher and Holly Hamilton host a pre-recorded, end-of-year episode of the show that puts the heart and soul into Sundays, bringing faith and ethics to the discussions that matter most. We reflect on a year when warnings of the risks facing humanity have regularly been in the news and examine the impact these themes could have on society as we ask: can a crisis bring us together? And, a year after Dame Sarah Mullally was formally elected as archbishop of Canterbury, we discuss what the future of the church could look like. We also hear the story of the Scottish teenager who could become a saint.

programme.title: Celebration Kitchen
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt is joined by chefs Gurdeep Loyal, Ravinder Bhogal and Manpreet Singh. Celebrity guests Ranvir Singh, Dr Ranj and Sathnam Sanghera celebrate the Sikh festival Guru Nanak Gurpurab.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: From the Golden Globes to the Emmys, it’s awards season on the show as Natasha Raskin Sharp marvels at movie memorabilia, all owned by a familiar face – Bargain Hunt expert and film fan Stephanie Connell. Steph shares with Natasha items from her own collection, including awards given to Sir John Gielgud and an original prop from 1970 film Julius Caesar, starring Charlton Heston. In a Brackley antiques centre, two teams hope to find some blockbuster buys of their own, helped by leading men Tim Weeks and Thomas Forrester. And in the grand finale at the auction in Derbyshire, auctioneer James Lewis gives his verdict on the teams’ items.

programme.desc: An anxious teacher starts a new job at an under-achieving school and quickly finds himself struggling to cope with a wild classroom assistant, a group of under-performing kids and his own very pregnant wife. He soon becomes embroiled in a madcap plan to enter a national Song for Christmas competition and finds himself embarking on a disastrous road trip in search of the competition venue - the Christmas Castle. Lost in the wilderness with a class of small children, a baby and a donkey, he has to stand up, face his fears and try to lead them not only to safety, but victory.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Charlotte Smith and Sean Fletcher are in the Ceiriog Valley in north Wales, meeting former clinical vet Claire Whittle, who took on an upland farm two years ago. Charlotte finds out why Claire made the leap into farming and what regenerative farming means to her, before helping with health and pregnancy checks on her cattle. Sean gets stuck into a cow pat to explore the hidden world of dung beetles and helps plant trees in a new agroforestry field. Meanwhile, Tom investigates changes that could be coming for the game bird shooting industry.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow comes from Alexandra Gardens in the heart of Cardiff, where treasures include a Maori pipe, a book listing wartime spies and a rare SAS medal collection. Ronnie Archer-Morgan is thrilled to see a pipe by a renowned Maori craftsman, whilst Geoffrey Munn is dazzled by a jewel-encrusted stick pin given as a gift from King Edward VII and Queen Alexandra. There are plenty of Welsh treasures to be found, including an autograph book featuring a Tom Jones signature and early concert ticket, and Lisa Lloyd challenges Fiona to spot the most valuable item in a group of three pieces of rare rugby memorabilia. Marc Allum is stunned to see a remarkable archive of First World War-era photographs documenting arrivals into Cardiff Docks, some of whom were suspected of being spies, and militaria expert Mark Smith is humbled by a group of medals and a cap badge belonging to one of the earliest members of the SAS. Fiona Bruce finds out about the long history of Alexandra Gardens as a war memorial when she meets Simon Weston, veteran of the Falklands conflict.

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing
programme.desc: It’s part two of the Blackpool spectacular, and we’re back in the Tower Ballroom for the results. The pros hit the dance floor for another dazzling group performance before two couples must dance again to try to keep their place in the competition. Who will dance for the final time in Blackpool? And who will return for an Instant Dance next weekend?

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc: A look at the surprising connections between the world's oceans, from the icy worlds of the poles to unexpected coasts closer to home.

programme.title: The Witch Farm
programme.desc: Summer 1989. Looking for a fresh start, Bill and his pregnant partner Liz move to a remote farmhouse in the idyllic Brecon Beacons with his teenage son Jonathan. Yet on the very first night, Liz hears footsteps on the landing. Before long, she and Jonathan are sharing disturbing dreams. And as strange events intensify, Bill and Liz are forced to accept a terrifying new reality.

programme.desc: A recovery truck ploughs into an SUV carrying a mother and daughter, sending it flying into another car. The driver insists he's done nothing wrong, but a bus dashcam holds crucial evidence. A minor moped collision sparks a claim for tens of thousands of pounds, and a fraud investigator uncovers suspicious connections. Could the claimant's own footage expose the scam? An HGV leaves a cyclist perilously short of room.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin, Dion and Martel check out auction property buys in Plymouth, Silsden in West Yorkshire and the village of Mytholmroyd near Hebden Bridge. The developers do a lot of the work themselves in the hope they can make a profit on their bricks-and-mortar investments.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: The teams are shopping in the mid-Wales town of Builth Wells, and Danny learns about a unique family business which immortalises rugby players and other Welsh icons in clay.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: Denise van Outen is stepping into the fight against fraud - and this time, it’s personal. After scammers stole thousands from her in a devious bank scam two years ago, Denise is teaming up with Scam Interceptors to turn the tables. In this special episode, airing as part of BBC Scam Safe week, Denise joins Rav Wilding and the team to expose the global web of criminals targeting UK victims, including those taking advantage of her identity. Using the same remote access tech scammers rely on, the team hacks the hackers to monitor their operations in real time, before confronting them. Denise also uses voice-changing technology to have fun at the scammers’ expense.

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives
programme.desc: When one of Nottingham’s oldest businesses is broken into, staff member Becca turns Miss Marple and manages to crack the case. Former police inspector Anton Sullivan shows two residents of the doorbell detective neighbourhood the elaborate lengths thieves will go to, to get their hands on your stuff. And Matt also hears from two friends whose life savings disappeared overnight when their food truck was stolen.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Nicki Chapman is in glorious Gloucestershire with Sam and Mandy, who are moving from a harbour town in Devon and making a fresh start in the countryside, with their two much-loved dogs coming along for the adventure. With £475,000 to spend, Nicki serves up a terrific selection of homes, but it’s the mystery house that really raises the stakes, with views so spectacular they feel like they’re standing on top of the world. From one grand outlook to another, Nicki gets an exclusive invitation to experience horticulture on a truly regal scale when she visits a garden quite literally fit for a king.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: The team help commemorate the victims of the Lockerbie bombing, automata expert Michael tackles a clockwork train, and Kirsten gets hands-on with medieval slipware pottery.

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp, assisted by Sarah Greene, hosts the quiz show where contestants race in moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers will stop them in their tracks. Five contestants - Amanda, Jamie, Iain, Namita and Chris - battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Vick Hope for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

After scammers stole thousands from her in a devious bank scam two years ago, Denise is teaming up with Scam Interceptors to turn the tables. In this special episode, airing as part of BBC Scam Safe week, Denise joins Rav Wilding and the team to expose the global web of criminals targeting UK victims, including those taking advantage of her identity. Using the same remote access tech scammers rely on, the team hacks the hackers to monitor their operations in real time, before confronting them. Denise also uses voice-changing technology to have fun at the scammers’ expense.

programme.title: The Marvellous Miniature Workshop
programme.desc: Sara Cox and the team meet Steven, a fourth-generation baker who longs to see his family’s beloved bakery brought back to life in miniature. Once the heart of local life, the business has since been lost to changing times. Can Lee Robinson capture the shopfront, the loaves and the legacy that meant everything to Steven’s family?

programme.title: The Witch Farm
programme.desc: The family receive a shockingly high electricity bill, and their animals start to behave oddly. Liz meets spiritualist Bethan at a mother and baby group. After a strained Christmas dinner, Jonathan admits he’s also seen a ghost. Liz and Bill beg Brecon Council for help, raising the suspicions of social services. Bethan offers to conduct a seance, leading to a shocking conclusion.

programme.title: The Traitors Ireland
programme.desc: The doors of Slane Castle have opened once again, with 23 new players entering The Traitors Ireland for its second season. The line-up features contestants from across the country, ranging in age from 24 to 61 and including teachers, a postal worker, a psychotherapist, a musician, a stay-at-home dad, an Irish Defence Forces member, and an actor and drama teacher. Hosted once again by Siobhán McSweeney, the players attempt to navigate a game built on trust, strategy and deception, forming alliances while trying to work out who among them they can believe.

programme.desc: A van delivery boss receives an alarming alert: one of his vehicles has crashed, and he can't reach the driver. The footage reveals no sign of braking before impact. An insurer tackles a bitter roundabout dispute involving a parent and baby, while in Liverpool, a driver overtakes a cyclist, then turns straight across their path. The cameras capture the danger and the clues to what went wrong.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: A very slick Sky impersonation scammer gives the team a difficult day as he uses multiple types of remote access to control a victim’s phone. With software installed allowing him to run their device, the team try every trick up their sleeve to intercept the scam before the devious criminal can buy himself gift cards.

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives
programme.desc: When burglars target Christine and Gary's shop, taking half-a-million pounds' worth of stock, it’s like something out of a heist movie. Former police inspector Anton Sullivan highlights a worrying new trend called car cannibalism, where thieves strip your car for parts. And we also hear how doggy doorbell detective Truman warns his owners that their high-end luxury car is being pinched from their driveway.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Seaside serenity beckons in Dorset as Sonali Shah helps Norman and Lynda swap city life in London for the calm of the coast. The fantastic line-up of properties includes a mystery house that die-hard fans of the show might just recognise. Sonali also takes a break from house hunting to unwind at a rejuvenating seaweed spa.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero. The boys answer a distress call from Swindon, where a plane-shaped bench paying tribute to the town’s aviation history is no longer fit to fly. A local woodworking group have taken on the task of fixing it, but they’re in need of some assistance from master carpenter Will. Meanwhile, Dom meets Tulsi, who has a Hindu holy scripture passed down from her grandmother that’s now so fragile it can’t be opened without further damage. It will take every trick in the book if paper conservator Angie is to get this beloved tome back to a state where the family can use it once again. One of the great joys of leaving the barn is the chance for our experts to meet some of the passionate makers around the country keeping heritage crafts alive. And few are as passionate as Chris, who is buzzing to teach Will all about the traditional way of making skeps, surprisingly strong, traditional bee hives made out of willow.

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp, assisted by Sarah Greene, hosts the quiz show where contestants race in moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers will stop them in their tracks. Five contestants - Laura, Olu, Jack, Jane, Luke - battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: The brainy quiz returns, but this time Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Hugh Dennis. As always, contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

His case is taken up by New Mexico lawyer Nancy Hollander, who is determined to take the US government to task for unlawful detention.

programme.desc: After the attack on his best friends and threats against his sister, Mobeen is armed, dangerous and out for revenge. But can he solve his problems without any bloodshed, or will they land him deeper in the criminal world he’s trying to escape. His attempts to make up for past mistakes see him pulled back into the world of unhinged crime boss Uncle Khan. Owing money to Khan (with deadly consequences if he doesn’t pay him back), Mobeen struggles to undertake his criminal orders under the watchful eye of Khan’s useless nephew Nav. Now living at Uncle Shady’s 'safe house', can Mobeen keep his family safe whilst staying out of jail? Or will the dark path he is being forced down lead to him paying the ultimate price?

Richard gives the old Chevrolet Lacetti a dignified send-off before he and Clarkson host a star-studded tea party to welcome in a shiny new Reasonably Priced Car.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May attempt to find a trio of cars which are equally at home on the racetrack as they are transporting a family to the shops, for a budget of £5,000. They end up with a BMW M3, a Mercedes 190E and a Ford Sierra Cosworth, which they put through their paces in Europe's home of speed, Germany. James also makes a rare visit to the Top Gear track to test a pair of Porsches - the 911 Sport Classic and Boxster Spyder - and Alastair Campbell is the star in the all-new reasonably priced car.

programme.title: Silent Witness

programme.desc: The BBC’s comedy talent search is back. More than a thousand comics applied, and just 30 made it through to the heats. This is the last of six, and five more acts are competing for the last place in this year’s grand final. The Box at Fargo Village, Coventry, will once again be converted into the BBC’s own New Comedy Club. Mancunian ray of sunshine Josh Jones is our host for the night. Joining him are the three judges – star of Ghosts and Taskmaster Kiell Smith-Bynoe, former NCA winner Dan Tiernan, and head judge, the multi-talented award-winning actor and comedian Amy Gledhill. Kwami Odoom, Stanley Magill, Harry Jenkins, Alasdair Wallace and Alana Jackson will each perform their set before the judges decide who will go through to the grand final. Since the awards launched in 1995, past finalists and winners have included Peter Kay, Joe Lycett, Lee Mack, Julian Barratt, Josie Long, Shappi Khorsandi, Romesh Ranganathan, Alan Carr, Russell Howard, Lee Ridley, Tom Allen, Lauren Pattison and Sarah Millican.

programme.title: Horrible Histories

It follows the young Mary as she stumbles from being a young girl in Scotland to queen in France, back to queen in Scotland and finally to Elizabeth I's public enemy number one - with a bit of Queenian Rhapsody thrown in for good measure! Meanwhile, across the world, we meet silver-nosed Danish scientist Tycho Brahe, and Mr H gives us his unique take on the epic Battle of Lepanto in another History's Craziest Fools. With, of course, our host Rattus to guide the way!

programme.title: The Holiday
programme.desc: Two women from different countries swap homes for the holidays to get away from their relationship issues.

programme.title: What We Did on Our Holiday
programme.desc: When Doug and Abi travel to Scotland for a birthday celebration, they have to try to hide the fact from their family that they are going through a divorce.

programme.title: Two Doors Down
programme.desc: When Eric raids the freezer after coming in from a night out, he leaves the door open and all the food inside defrosts. Beth decides to cook everything at once and invite Cathy, Colin, Ian, Jaz, Christine and Sophie over to eat it all. Everything goes well until Cathy urges Colin to go next door and get something out of their freezer to replace the defrosted food, a whole Scottish salmon.

programme.title: 40 Hidden Music Treasures at the BBC
programme.desc: Expect the unexpected on this journey through the BBC’s magical music archives, a Top 40 with a difference. In a Top of the Pops-free-zone, these are the surprising songs and rare performances that aren't seen every day, taken from shows that may have been forgotten - but that definitely deserve to see daylight once again. And whilst some of the musical moments may have been hidden away, the talents involved have always been prominent - ranging from Jimi Hendrix to MC Hammer, from Dusty to Tammy, and from The Beach Boys to The Pet Shop Boys.

programme.title: Celebrity Race Across the World
programme.desc: The third leg of the race sees the teams leave behind the ancient jungles of Borneo to reach the island of Sulawesi, an Indonesian wonderland that lies far from the tourist trail. But with the end of Ramadan fast approaching, the teams must negotiate the crowds heading home for Eid al-Fitr.

programme.title: Bill's Included
programme.desc: When Bill’s wife walks out on him for the gardener, he’s left lonely and broke. In the hope of turning his life around, he lets out his spare rooms to four students. Bill is thrilled to meet his new housemates: Christian, Zahra, Hettie, and James. But when Christian keeps leaving the fridge door open, Bill has to come up with a scheme to get it shut without ruining his image as a relaxed, fun landlord. Bill’s best mate, Drew, gives him the idea to deploy an anonymous suggestions box, but this backfires when the students’ requests lead to the worst night’s sleep of his life. Bill’s neighbour and secret crush, Siobhan, suggests sending over her intimidating husband, Martin, to complain on Bill’s behalf, but when this ruse is exposed, Bill fears the students will leave him, just like his wife did. He’s grateful to learn that not only do they have nowhere else to live but they forgive him, since university is all about starting over. For better or worse, his new life truly has begun.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Hamza Yassin heads to a secret location in Scotland’s Southern Uplands to join a dedicated team on an exciting mission to protect the fastest animal in the world - the peregrine falcon. Getting up close to three chicks, he discovers how DNA sampling is helping to tackle the theft of these remarkable birds. Along the way, the programme revisits memorable Countryfile wildlife encounters, from dolphins off Anglesey to spectacular starling murmurations at Newport Wetlands.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: A special episode from north Sutherland at the top of the Scottish mainland. Dougie steps out into the Flow Country, a vast expanse of blanket peat bog, where he charts the changes in its land use and its recent designation as a Unesco World Heritage site. Arlene catches up with sheep farmer Joyce Campbell to see how she has made the switch from traditional hill farming to regenerative agriculture. Arlene also visits Strath Halladale, where she meets a man who gave up city life to run the family croft 37 years ago. She finds out how he has built a thriving timber business and brought jobs to the area. And at Loch Hope, Leanna meets the biologists working to protect precious sea trout populations.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Indonesian cook and gardener Dina Watt takes us from garden fork to table fork. Dina cultivates to cook in her Banchory garden, creating tasty and innovative dishes with her homegrown produce and adding an Indonesian twist to her local crops. Dina also introduces us to the Maxwell Centre in the heart of Coldside, Dundee, where they teach local children to grow, care for, harvest and then eat what they produce.

programme.title: A Cook Abroad
programme.desc: Scottish chef Tony Singh travels to India, the country of his ancestors, to trace his family roots and discover whether his mum's Punjabi cooking is the real deal. He begins his journey in Amritsar, which is draped in lights for the festival of Diwali, before braving the treacherous Grand Trunk Road to Delhi, a place Tony has only ever visited twice. Along the way, he fulfils a boyhood dream to meet the Nihang, nomadic Sikh warriors whose cooking techniques are legendary. He receives an exclusive invite to eat and cook with a Maharaja and, as his waistline tightens thanks to the rich Punjabi diet, he burns off the calories at Bollysweat, the fitness phenomenon taking Delhi by storm. As Tony gets under the skin of Punjabi ways, he discovers how the Sikh religion and the region's troubled past have created a food and culture like no other. He ends his epic adventure at the ancestral home in Delhi, where his 93-year-old uncle Ameer opens a window on his family history he will never forget.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: Paris is home to more award-winning pastry chefs than anywhere else in the world. Here, the day revolves around patisserie. Morning begins with the buttery flakes of a croissant. At midday, a baguette tucked under the arm signals lunch. And by the afternoon, mouthwatering sweet treats are savoured like miniature works of art. Resistance is futile, and Eva is seduced by the Paris-Brest, a rum baba, the macaron, a mango cake and dahlia, to name just a few.

programme.title: The Man Who Never Was
programme.desc: Espionage thriller in which a British intelligence officer plans an elaborate hoax in the spring of 1943 to fool the Germans into thinking the Allies are about to invade Greece, not Sicily. The plan calls for the navy to float a dead body carrying false identification and information so that the Germans will pick it up. The first part of the mission succeeds, but will the Nazis take the bait?

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: In Scotland, Martel encounters a house with a safety order attached to it, which means certain rooms can’t be accessed. Owain is in south Wales to see a sizeable unit with lots of development potential. In Lincolnshire, Dion is doing all he can to escape the rain!

programme.title: Women's Super League
programme.desc: Coverage of the Women's Super League clash between Arsenal and West Ham United.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This edition of Flog It! comes from Longleat in Wiltshire, home to the world-famous safari park and 16th-century Longleat House. In this rather special show, Paul Martin is joined by experts Michael Baggott and Claire Rawle. Whilst picking out a selection of interesting antiques and collectables to be sold at a local auction, Claire spots an unusual Tibetan teapot. This leads to the momentous discovery of other of Tibetan artefacts belonging to the same owner, a collection of controversial historical significance which all ends up going under the hammer. With worldwide interest in these objects, will the Flog It! record for the highest value item sold at auction be broken when the sale goes on to raise thousands of pounds? Paul also gets the chance to explore Longleat House, learning more about its controversial creator and wonderful Elizabethan architecture.

programme.title: Celebrity Race Across the World
programme.desc: In the fourth leg, the teams enter a new frontier, Australia. The sixth largest country on the planet and home to eight distinct climate zones, it’s a land of extreme contrasts. Language barriers may have evaporated, but in their place is a new challenge, the budget, as the country delivers all teams a financial reality check. The teams descend on the fourth checkpoint in the tightest race yet, with a foot race to the sign-in book.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: Spring is in the air, bringing newborn livestock. In North Uist, Carianne spends her days on the tiny island of Vallay in search of new Highland calves. When one calf is discovered without a mother, Carianne must turn detective to reunite them. In Inverkip, Rachel and Camy are heading to the hills to help any of their Cheviot sheep in need of a midwife. And in South Ayrshire, the Barclay family are working round the clock to ensure their flock of Beltex ewes safely deliver this year’s crop of lambs.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: Eva takes a boat trip down the Seine with chef Eric Ripert and writer Lindsey Tramuta. Together, they explore the story of French gastronomy through a seven-course fine dining meal. At the heart of this delicious story is one man – Auguste Escoffier. He dominated every aspect of gastronomy, inventing and improving hundreds of classic dishes, bringing order to chaos in the kitchen with his military-style brigade and revolutionising front of house. Escoffier put French haute cuisine on the global map.

programme.title: Ireland with Simon Reeve
programme.desc: Starting at the spectacular Giant's Causeway in Northern Ireland, Simon travels down the east coast to the great and rapidly changing cities of Belfast and Dublin. He ends his journey in the stunning Wicklow Mountains.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob travel to County Tyrone to fish at Baronscourt Estate, hoping to catch a pike of a lifetime. They have access to two beautiful and secluded loughs, set in over 130 acres of rolling countryside, and the private use of one rowing boat – what could possibly go wrong? Pike are wily fish, always hiding in the dark reeds and waiting to ambush their prey. Bob has a fail-safe method to try, but will the duo be able to outwit the elusive creatures?

programme.title: A Course Called Ireland
programme.desc: After weeks of travelling, filming and constant attention, life on the road is taking its toll on Bill. With brothers Joel and Johnny along for the ride, family offers an escape from fame. The Murrays reflect on losing their father young, and how caddying and golf bound nine siblings together. By the time they reach Cruit Island in Donegal, family reflection gives way to golfing rivalry.

programme.title: Uncanny
programme.desc: Lindsey and her family move to a new-build house on the Isle of Thanet in Kent. For years, they live happily at the property, but then their quiet lives are suddenly rocked by a series of terrifying events: repeated footsteps every night, door handles that move by themselves and the appearance of a cloaked, hunched, shadowy figure. Who is the figure? Could the answers lie beneath their feet?

When they arrive, Rose's parents are genial and welcoming to him, but the more time he spends with them and their quiet, obedient servants, the more Chris feels that something is very, very wrong.

programme.title: Blue Velvet
programme.desc: When the discovery of a severed ear in a field leads a small-town college student to a bewitching nightclub singer, he finds himself lost in a dark underworld of fear and depravity. A disturbing, unique exploration of the dark side of American suburbia from director David Lynch.

programme.title: Question Time
programme.desc: Fiona Bruce presents an hour of debate from Worthing, with politicians, commentators and members of the public. The UK government has backed plans by former minister Alan Milburn for sweeping reforms to prevent 'losing a generation' of young people to a life on benefits, and this week’s EU-UK talks are going 'down to the wire' according to Downing Street. Fiona Bruce presents an hour of topical debate from Worthing, debating Neets, rejoining the EU and old Brexit wounds, the housing crisis and Labour’s housing targets, and which politician, in the panel’s opinion, would make a good Bond villain. On the panel are Labour’s former foreign secretary David Lammy; the Conservatives’ shadow work and pensions minister Joe Robertson; Adrian Ramsay of the Green Party; the entrepreneur Alex Depledge; and the Times columnist Fraser Nelson.

programme.desc: Martha is annoyed after Kurt steals their joint credit for locating Kamilla, and she vows to gain access to the scientist alone. A competitive Kurt promises to do the same. Eager for a win, Martha and Kurt attempt to insinuate their way into Friedrich’s confidence to find Greta. Stung by his reaction, Martha steals a prized possession.

programme.title: This is BBC Two

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles visits Nottingham’s Gothic revival cathedral to learn how conservators are revealing 19th-century artwork under decades of plaster and paint. Designed in 1842 by architect Augustus Pugin, the cathedral’s interior was whitewashed in the 1960s. Pugin is widely admired for his work on some of Britain’s most famous buildings, including the Palace of Westminster. Conservator Ana Logreira shows Eric how they are using digitally created stencils to renovate the cathedral’s historic interior. At Southwell Racecourse in Nottinghamshire, red team uncle and niece Russ and Lily are up against twin sisters Angie and Tamsin in blue. With just 60 minutes to buy three items, Russ makes an early pit stop at a stall selling boxed toy cars. Meanwhile, a marcasite brooch catches the sisters’ attention, but expert Irita Marriott isn’t convinced it will dazzle the bidders. Trying to hammer out a profit for the teams in Nottingham is auctioneer Hettie Jago, who has her eye on the jewellery among the lots.

programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family and friends Amy, JP, Nic and Alan – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

Chef Julie Lin is in Dundee, finding out how bakers keep up with demand around the clock.

Will uncovers some salacious etchings by a very famous artist, while Christina finds a unique autograph book, but will it reach for the stars or languish at the bottom of the bill? Plus BBC Eye reveals new evidence showing how scouts, agencies and powerful fashion figures helped Jeffrey Epstein gain access to young women after his conviction for sex offences. And BBC Urdu joins women in Pakistan who are challenging traditional barriers by taking to the road on motorbikes, gaining new independence in a country where riding has long been considered off-limits to many women.

She has a close shave in the dreaded Council of Ten's torture chamber, discovers a 24-carat gold staircase that leads to one of the biggest rooms in Europe, and encounters hidden doors and secret messages.

Eventually, he is sent packing, and Stephen reveals his mother does not play bingo. Back in Belfast, Jade, Tom, Perri and Adam spot a row outside shops where young people say their money has been stolen by a woman. CCTV suggests the man she is with may also have headbutted a passer-by. The man violently resists arrest, fighting, spitting and shouting sectarian abuse at Tom and Adam. A reworking of Bill Gallagher’s hard-hitting thriller for the big screen.

Will time have healed old wounds, or will old rivalries still burn brightly?

programme.title: Then She Found Me

programme.title: Touchy Feely

programme.desc: When Doug gets into a fist fight with a hockey thug, an onlooking coach recruits him despite of his lack of any hockey playing ability. Written by Jay Baruchel & Evan Goldberg, co-writer of Superbad & Pineapple Express.

programme.title: Tucker & Dale Vs. Evil
programme.desc: Tucker and Dale, two best friends on vacation at their dilapidated mountain house, are mistaken for murderous backwoods hillbillies by a group of obnoxious, preppy college kids.

programme.title: Drinking Buddies
